newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's September oil output up 5.5 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Peru's September oil output up 5.5 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Peru produced an average 123,761 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil in September, up 5.5 percent from 117,337 bpd the same month last year, Energy and Mines Ministry said Monday.
Peru's average production in the first nine months was an average 119,754 bpd, the ministry added without giving a comparative figure for 1995.
Total oil production was 3.7 million barrels in September, and 32.8 million barrels in the first nine months.
Natural gas output in September averaged 24.410 million cubic feet per day, the ministry said. Gas production in the first nine months was an average 119,754 bpd.

Oil production in Peru dropped 4.36 percent last year to an average of 121,762 barrels a day (bpd). Officials have said the drop in Peru's oil output is due to the depletion of old wells and poor drilling results looking for new oil.
Occidental Petroleum Corp, Petro-Tech S.A., Argentina's Pluspetrol and state oil company Petroperu S.A. account for more than 90 percent of Peru's total oil output.
